sectors.trend: Brent nears $100, WTI past $101; US-Iran tit-for-tat strikes and Saudi infrastructure attacks tighten supply. Hedge funds aggressively long fuels. ExxonMobil's 20th Angola discovery (2.7B barrels) offers long-term supply relief.
sectors.implications: Inflation reacceleration risk; margin pressure on airlines, transport, and consumer discretionary. Energy equities and E&P names benefit. Nat-gas remains pressured by abundant US supply.

sectors.trend: Nvidia earnings Sept 10 as key catalyst; Apple foldable iPhone launch but 2 MacBook cancellations; Qualcomm-Amazon $15B data-center deal; Google Cloud AI chip claims; Anthropic researcher quits over AI safety; quantum stocks climb on CHIPS Act funding.
sectors.implications: AI capex cycle continues but fragmentation risk rises. Semiconductor names (NVDA, QCOM) face binary event risk. Quantum and AI infrastructure remain structurally bullish.

sectors.trend: China-US 10Y yield gap at record; Bessent's rate intervention backfires; 5/1 ARM breaks 7%; 3-year auction sees strong demand; CD rates up to 4.35% APY; mortgage rates inch higher on oil-driven inflation.

sectors.implications: Gold pullback is tactical, not structural. Central-bank buying supports medium-term bid. Uranium and agricultural commodities offer diversification.

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish-to-neutral. Oil above $100 and US-Iran strikes drive inflation fears, pressuring equities (Asian sell-off confirmed). Nvidia earnings create binary volatility. Bessent's failed rate intervention undermines Fed credibility. Trade war with Canada adds tariff pass-through. Expect elevated VIX, sector rotation into energy/defense, and continued bond yield volatility. 3-5% equity drawdown risk if oil breaks $110.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. AI capex supercycle (Qualcomm-Amazon, Google Cloud, quantum CHIPS Act) supports tech earnings through 2027. EM convergence trades (Hungary euro, SE Asia, India) offer 12-18 month alpha. Energy transition (Angola, Namibia uranium, US battery supply chain) creates structural winners. Inflation likely moderates post-Iran de-escalation, enabling rate cuts by Q1 2027. Consumer squeeze (insurance, tariffs) is cyclical, not structural.
